comparison: Perfect agreement on SAXS data showing enhanced conformational dynamics in AL-LCs. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED with identical claim sets (C7-C9, C47-C54). Reviewers explicitly affirm the finding as 'expertly recorded' and 'convincing evidence,' though one requests p-value verification.

Strong disagreement on HDX-MS validation strength. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED citing robust orthogonal validation with >90% coverage (C79-C94), while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to limited sample size (only 3 AL and 1 non-AL proteins yielding useful data) and questions about consistency with MD simulations.

Agreement on uncertainty regarding A40G mutation analysis. Both rate UNCERTAIN with identical claim sets (C101-C106). OpenEval notes lack of experimental validation and contradictory evidence from M10; peer reviewers request deeper contextualization with prior literature and note speculative language.

Agreement on MD simulation evidence for H state as major finding. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes computational robustness (120-180 µs simulations, convergent duplicates) for claims C10-C12, C55-C57, C65-C74. Peer reviewers affirm 'clever M&M simulations' and 'novel finding' but note lack of physical mechanistic insights. Peer review also includes CL-CL interface claims (C75-C78) that OpenEval addresses separately.

OpenEval separately evaluates CL-CL interface heterogeneity (C75-C78) as SUPPORTED with clear free energy surface evidence. Peer reviewers group these claims with broader H state findings (R2) and rate SUPPORTED, though they note limited mechanistic understanding.

Agreement on RMSF analysis and computational approach quality. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for appropriate caution in interpretation (C58-C64), noting flexibility differences may reflect CDR length rather than amyloidogenic properties. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED for computational methods but note 'lack of physical insights,' affirming the descriptive nature acknowledged by OpenEval.

Agreement on conceptual framework integration. Both rate SUPPORTED for synthesis with prior literature (C116-C118). OpenEval emphasizes conformational dynamics over stability as key distinction; peer reviewers affirm therapeutic promise and integration quality but suggest deeper mutation analysis would strengthen therapeutic relevance.

Partial overlap on therapeutic implications (C119). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting lack of experimental validation for druggability. Peer reviewers include C119 in broader SUPPORTED evaluation (R6) stating 'Stabilization of the CL-CL interface is a good idea,' but also note need for deeper analysis to strengthen therapeutic relevance.

OpenEval evaluates sequence alignment findings (C107-C110) as SUPPORTED, documenting mutations restricted to VL domains in both CDR and framework regions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific claims.

OpenEval evaluates Ramachandran analysis (C114-C115) as SUPPORTED for appropriately reporting negative results on frustrated CDRs hypothesis (C112-C113). No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific claims.

Peer reviewers express UNCERTAIN evaluation regarding sample size limitations (C39-C46), repeatedly noting this affects generalizability and HDX data quality. OpenEval does not provide a separate evaluation specifically addressing sample size concerns as a distinct result.
